Which IR features each writer expresses: the six stable ones, and PPTX, which is still [experimental](output-formats.qmd#experimental-formats). Every cell is *measured*: the test renders a probe table, reads the output back with a format-specific reader (cell by cell: weight, slant, decoration, color, size, font, fill, alignment, borders; for the table as a whole, its language and direction) and checks the feature is there — and doesn't leak into neighboring cells. The test fails whenever a measurement disagrees with this page.

✓ supported · ✗ not yet (the format can express it) · ⊘ the format can't (portably) express it. Numbers refer to the notes below. A table that uses a feature its format lacks gets a warning saying where, with the note as its reason: see [Validation](../schema/validation.qmd#warnings).

| Feature | IR | HTML | LaTeX | Typst | RTF | DOCX | XLSX | PPTX |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bold | `font_weight: bold` (or ≥ 600) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| italic | `font_style: italic` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| underline | `text_decoration: underline` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| strikethrough | `text_decoration: line-through` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| text-color | `color` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| font-size | `font_size` (20px = 15pt) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| font-family | `font_family` (a named family, not just monospace) | ✓ | ⊘<sup>1</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| text-transform | `text_transform: uppercase` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| fill | `background_color` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| cell-align | `text_align` on a cell | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| column-align | a column's `align` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| vertical-align | `vertical_align: bottom` (beside a taller cell) | ✓ | ⊘<sup>2</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| border | `border` (2px solid red bottom) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| border-styles | border styles dashed, dotted | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| border-double | border style double | ✓ | ✓ | ⊘<sup>3</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| column-style | a column's `style_id` (cascades to its cells) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| row-style | a row's `style_id` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| striping | `row_striping` (every second body row filled) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| conditional-style | `styles.conditionals` (row parity) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| style-composition | `styles.compositions` (extends + overrides) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| styled-run | inline `styled_text` (part of a cell bold) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| footnote-mark | footnote marks as superscript | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| title | `header.title` and `header.subtitle` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| notes | footnotes and source notes | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| line-styles | a `style_id` on the title, subtitle, header lines, group labels (and their fill) and notes | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| normal-weight | `font_weight: normal` on what a format draws bold by default (column labels, the title, a group label, a run in a bold cell) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| normal-style | `font_style: normal` on a run in an italic cell or line | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| image | an image (a PNG `data:` URI, 32×16px = 24×12pt) | ✓ | ⊘<sup>4</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ⊘<sup>5</sup> |
| raw-html | a `raw` HTML node's markup (`<b>`, `<i>`, a `style` attribute's `color`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| lang | `config.lang`, the table's language | ✓ | ⊘<sup>6</sup> | ✓ | ✗<sup>7</sup> | ✓ | ⊘<sup>8</sup> | ✓ |
| rtl | `config.dir: rtl`, columns and text right to left | ✓ | ⊘<sup>9</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**Notes**

1. a named system font needs XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX with fontspec; the output also targets pdfLaTeX (monospace families map to `\texttt`)
2. a tabular row sets its cells on one baseline; `m`/`b` columns align whole columns, not single cells
3. Typst strokes have no double line; a double border is drawn solid
4. a LaTeX fragment can't carry an image's data (`\includegraphics` reads a file): an image shows its alt text
5. PowerPoint text (a table cell, or the text box of a title or note) holds no pictures: an image shows its alt text
6. a language is the document's, set up by babel or polyglossia in the preamble the table goes into
7. RTF names a language by its Windows language id (`\lang`), which the writer doesn't yet map language tags to
8. a spreadsheet's cells have no language
9. right to left needs the bidirectional support of babel or polyglossia, set up in the document's preamble; the table is written left to right

Structure — spans, hidden columns, stub columns, hidden column labels, group labels and summary rows — is verified separately for every writer by the grid invariant: each output is read back as a grid and compared with the IR's.
